However, when the "C" form mechanism started on-line effective from 01.04.2010, the defendant started defaulting in the production of "C" forms to the plaintiff within the stipulated period as required.

One of the signs of the defendant's default was when he furnished a manual "C" form purportedly signed by the Commercial Tax Department on 15.9.2010,
for the period from April to June 2010.

The said form was unacceptable in the light of the circular issued by the Government of Pondicherry dated https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 27.08.2010 and this "C" form was returned by the plaintiff to the defendant with a request that the "C" form should be obtained by him on-line by submitting details on the prescribed website and thereafter duly furnished to the plaintiff for filing with the plaintiff's corresponding Assessing Officer at Chennai.

(xiii) The plaintiff has the reason to believe that the defendant exploited the situation not only to the disadvantage of the plaintiff, but also to the Government Exchequer by not paying the sales tax as required.

The immediate result of the default committed by the defendant exposed the plaintiff to a liability of Rs.8,24,67,463.69 Ps, which they would be obliged to pay to the Sales Tax Department at Chennai when the assessments are taken up for finalization.

This is not an instance where the plaintiff will have to wait for the assessment to be completed, as the non-production of "C" forms would automatically and unavoidably oblige the plaintiff to pay the higher rate of tax, including interest and penalty, due to the fact that the deadlines applicable for the foregone quarters had already expired and the C Forms had not been filed by the plaintiff solely due to the unlawful refusal of the defendant to furnish the same.

(xiv) The cause of action for these proceedings has arisen at Chennai within the jurisdiction of this Court from where the plaintiff is assessed to sales tax and all its returns and other sales tax formalities are completed in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the Office of the Fast Track Circle - 4,

The defendant filed a written statement wherein it has been stated as follows :
(i) As per Clause 19 of the DPSL agreement dated 08.3.2008 executed between the parties, any dispute or suit or action or proceeding arising from the DPSL agreement or the breach thereof should be subject to the jurisdiction of the Courts in Bombay.
When the parties have contractually agreed to subject themselves to the jurisdiction of Courts in Bombay, the jurisdiction of this Court automatically stands ousted.
Therefore, no cause of action having arisen before this Court and the above suit ought to be dismissed by this Court.

(ii) As admitted in the Plaint, even the supplies to the defendant were effected from the plaintiff 's installation at Karur, which is outside the jurisdiction of this Court and hence, the above Suit should not lie before this https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Court and ought to be dismissed in limine.
Even if the supplies were made from Tondiarpet, the same will not confer jurisdiction as the issue is non issuance of C Forms from Puducherry.
(iii) The suit is liable to be dismissed by this Court on the ground that it is premature.

The assessment of the plaintiff was not taken up by the Department as on the date of filing of the suit and therefore, the liability of the plaintiff to make the payment to the Department has not crystallised.
The aforesaid position is true even as admitted by the plaintiff in the plaint.

The suit has been filed in anticipation of the demand that will be levied by the Department when the assessment of the plaintiff is finalised and therefore, there is no cause of action in filing the above suit.
As on the date of fling the suit, the plaintiff has not suffered any loss.
(iv) The C Forms were illegally withheld by the Commercial Taxes Department for alleged tax arrears of the defendant under the Pondicherry Value Added Tax Act, 2007 for certain years.

The defendant disputed the tax liability and writ appeals filed by the defendant along with the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis restoration petitions filed by the defendant are pending before this Court.

(v) The above suit that has been filed claiming for recovery of a sum of Rs.8,24,67,436.69/- towards compensation in lieu of non-furnishing of C Forms, which have not been paid by the plaintiff even as per the averments in the plaint, is premature and liable to be dismissed in limine.
(vi) The suit is not sustainable for non-joinder of necessary parties.
The plaintiff made certain averments about the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry Tax Authorities.
But, they have not been arrayed as parties to substantiate the claims.
The factum of turnover, assessment, manual or electronic form can all be addressed only by the Statutory Authorities.
Hence, they are necessary parties.
Since the plaintiff failed to add them as parties, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
(vii) The averment that the supply was effected from Chennai in tankers designated by the Defendant was denied.
It is only at certain instances the supply was effected through the vehicles designated by the defendant.

(j) Under the Sales Tax Act, the "C" form is essential for availing concessional sales tax rates on interstate sales.
The "C" form is issued by the purchasing dealer to the selling dealer, certifying that the goods are being purchased for resale or use in the course of interstate trade.
This allows the seller to charge a reduced rate of tax.
If the "C" form is not provided, the seller is required to pay the higher rate of tax, which can lead to financial penalties and interest.

The civil suit in this case is maintainable because the plaintiff is not challenging the tax assessment, but rather seeking recovery for damages caused by the defendant's non- compliance with a contractual obligation to provide the "C" forms.
The issue at hand is the failure of the defendant to fulfill its duty, which directly led to the plaintiff incurring a higher tax liability.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since this is purely a matter relating to non-payment of commercial tax and non-furnishing of mandatory 'C Forms by the defendant to the plaintiff, the consequent severe prejudice being suffered by the plaintiff on account of non furnishing of the mandatory C Forms to the Assessing Authorities within Chennai and the pursuant tax consequences being faced in Chennai by the plaintiff, no cause of action has arisen within the jurisdiction of the Courts in Mumbai, and the Clause conferring jurisdiction of the Mumbai Courts would not be attracted in the circumstances of the case.
Even if the supplies were made from Tondiarpet, the same will not confer jurisdiction as the issue is non issuance of C Forms from Puducherry.
(iii) The suit is liable to be dismissed by this Court on the ground that it is premature.
The assessment of the plaintiff was not taken up by the Department as on the date of filing of the suit and therefore, the liability of the plaintiff to make the payment to the Department has not crystallised.
The suit has been filed in anticipation of the demand that will be levied by the Department when the assessment of the plaintiff is finalised and therefore, there is no cause of action in filing the above suit.
(iv) The C Forms were illegally withheld by the Commercial Taxes Department for alleged tax arrears of the defendant under the Pondicherry Value Added Tax Act, 2007 for certain years.
(vi) The suit is not sustainable for non-joinder of necessary parties.
The factum of turnover, assessment, manual or electronic form can all be addressed only by the Statutory Authorities.
Hence, they are necessary parties.
Since the plaintiff failed to add them as parties, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
(vii) The averment that the supply was effected from Chennai in tankers designated by the Defendant was denied.
